subject: multinomial logit with INLA - estimation of probabilities

messages.author: a1380c07d45cdb8b
messages.subject: multinomial logit with INLA - estimation of probabilities
parts:
Hi everyone.
I have a categorical variable X with I>2 outcomes, and I need to estimate the probabilities p(xi) allowing for covariates and/or temporal/spatial dependence.

I found the tutorial about the multinomial logit model in INLA (by Francesco Serafini), which I believe does what I am looking for.
Link to the tutorial I have:
https://www.dropbox.com/s/9sz5m1vabrqez5x/tutorial-multinomial-inla.pdf?dl=0

The problem is, as the tutorial says, that I get "pretty bad estimates for the gammas". This implies that I get bad estimates for the probabilities (even in the simplest case of independence, everything looks shifted).
This is the link to my code, in case someone wants to have a look
https://www.dropbox.com/s/a17ko4vmphx2lge/02_covariateCAT.R?dl=0

What can I do if I need to obtain good estimates for the probabilities?

Alternatively, do I have other options for estimating the probabilities of a categorical variable?

Thank you very much for your help!

Is that version the same as the vignette in the package? Make sure you have a recent version as well.

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] multinomial logit with INLA - estimation of probabilities
parts:
there is no way out to get 'better' estimates unless you know more.

please use R-4.0 and a recent version, check the vignette, and do a
simulation study under simular conditions to verify.

H
